"""

from __future__ import annotations

from fractions import Fraction
from itertools import permutations, product
from typing import Callable, Dict, FrozenSet, Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Basic types
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Coord = int                      # a coordinate i in I
Symbol = int                     # a symbol a in A
String = Tuple[Symbol, ...]      # a full proof string u : I -> A (indexed by position)
PartialView = Tuple[object, ...] # a partial assignment, None off the query set
QuerySet = FrozenSet[Coord]
Transcript = Tuple[object, object, PartialView, object]


def restrict_to(query: QuerySet, f: String) -> PartialView:
    """The partial view f|_T : None outside T, f(i) inside T."""
    return tuple(f[i] if i in query else None for i in range(len(f)))


def opened_support(view: PartialView) -> List[int]:
    """Coordinates on which a partial view is defined."""
    return [i for i, a in enumerate(view) if a is not None]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A committed local-oracle protocol
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class CommittedOracle:
    """A committed local-oracle protocol over finite randomness spaces.

    com        : (String, Rc) -> C
    open_info  : (String, Rc, QuerySet) -> O
    queries    : Rv -> QuerySet         with |Q(r)| <= qbound
    proof      : P -> String
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        n_coords: int,
        com: Callable[[String, object], object],
        open_info: Callable[[String, object, QuerySet], object],
        queries: Callable[[object], QuerySet],
        qbound: int,
        proof: Callable[[object], String],
        prover_rand: Sequence[object],
        commit_rand: Sequence[object],
        verifier_rand: Sequence[object],
    ) -> None:
        self.n_coords = n_coords
        self.com = com
        self.open_info = open_info
        self.queries = queries
        self.qbound = qbound
        self.proof = proof
        self.P = list(prover_rand)
        self.Rc = list(commit_rand)
        self.Rv = list(verifier_rand)
        for r in self.Rv:
            assert len(self.queries(r)) <= self.qbound, "query bound violated"

    # -- transcripts -------------------------------------------------------

    def real_transcript(self, p: object, rho: object, r: object) -> Transcript:
        u = self.proof(p)
        T = self.queries(r)
        return (self.com(u, rho), r, restrict_to(T, u), self.open_info(u, rho, T))

    def sim_transcript(
        self, sim: Callable[[object, object], String], s: object, rho: object, r: object
    ) -> Transcript:
        u = sim(r, s)
        T = self.queries(r)
        return (self.com(u, rho), r, restrict_to(T, u), self.open_info(u, rho, T))

    # -- exact distributions ----------------------------------------------

    def real_distribution(self) -> Dict[Transcript, Fraction]:
        total = len(self.P) * len(self.Rc) * len(self.Rv)
        counts: Dict[Transcript, int] = {}
        for p, rho, r in product(self.P, self.Rc, self.Rv):
            tau = self.real_transcript(p, rho, r)
            counts[tau] = counts.get(tau, 0) + 1
        return {t: Fraction(c, total) for t, c in counts.items()}

    def sim_distribution(
        self, sim: Callable[[object, object], String], sim_rand: Sequence[object]
    ) -> Dict[Transcript, Fraction]:
        total = len(sim_rand) * len(self.Rc) * len(self.Rv)
        counts: Dict[Transcript, int] = {}
        for s, rho, r in product(sim_rand, self.Rc, self.Rv):
            tau = self.sim_transcript(sim, s, rho, r)
            counts[tau] = counts.get(tau, 0) + 1
        return {t: Fraction(c, total) for t, c in counts.items()}

    # -- the two resources -------------------------------------------------

    def fiber_count(self, u: String, T: QuerySet, c: object, o: object) -> int:
        """#{rho : com(u,rho)=c and open(u,rho,T)=o}."""
        return sum(
            1
            for rho in self.Rc
            if self.com(u, rho) == c and self.open_info(u, rho, T) == o
        )

    def hides_unopened(self, messages: Iterable[String]) -> bool:
        """Check Definition: for all T and all u,v agreeing on T, the fibre
        counts of u and v coincide for every (c,o).  (This is exactly the
        consequence of the hiding bijection that the composition theorem uses,
        and by a counting argument it is equivalent to it over finite Rc.)"""
        msgs = list(messages)
        all_T = [self.queries(r) for r in self.Rv]
        for T in all_T:
            for u, v in product(msgs, msgs):
                if any(u[i] != v[i] for i in T):
                    continue
                pairs = {(self.com(u, rho), self.open_info(u, rho, T)) for rho in self.Rc}
                pairs |= {(self.com(v, rho), self.open_info(v, rho, T)) for rho in self.Rc}
                for (c, o) in pairs:
                    if self.fiber_count(u, T, c, o) != self.fiber_count(v, T, c, o):
                        return False
        return True

    def simulates_opened(
        self, sim: Callable[[object, object], String], sim_rand: Sequence[object]
    ) -> bool:
        """Check  N_real(r,t)*|S| == N_sim(r,t)*|P|  for all r and all views t."""
        nP, nS = len(self.P), len(sim_rand)
        for r in self.Rv:
            T = self.queries(r)
            real: Dict[PartialView, int] = {}
            for p in self.P:
                t = restrict_to(T, self.proof(p))
                real[t] = real.get(t, 0) + 1
            fake: Dict[PartialView, int] = {}
            for s in sim_rand:
                t = restrict_to(T, sim(r, s))
                fake[t] = fake.get(t, 0) + 1
            for t in set(real) | set(fake):
                if real.get(t, 0) * nS != fake.get(t, 0) * nP:
                    return False
        return True


def distributions_equal(
    d1: Dict[Transcript, Fraction], d2: Dict[Transcript, Fraction]
) -> bool:
    return all(d1.get(t, Fraction(0)) == d2.get(t, Fraction(0)) for t in set(d1) | set(d2))


def statistical_distance(
    d1: Dict[Transcript, Fraction], d2: Dict[Transcript, Fraction]
) -> Fraction:
    return sum(
        abs(d1.get(t, Fraction(0)) - d2.get(t, Fraction(0))) for t in set(d1) | set(d2)
    ) / 2


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ingredient 1: the coordinate-wise one-time pad
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def otp_com(modulus: int) -> Callable[[String, String], String]:
    def com(u: String, rho: String) -> String:
        return tuple((a + b) % modulus for a, b in zip(u, rho))

    return com


def otp_open(u: String, rho: String, T: QuerySet) -> PartialView:
    """Opening data = the pad revealed on the queried set."""
    return restrict_to(T, rho)


def demo_one_time_pad_hiding() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("1.  THE ONE-TIME PAD PERFECTLY HIDES UNOPENED COORDINATES")
    print("=" * 78)
    m, n = 3, 3  # alphabet Z/3, three coordinates
    pads: List[String] = [tuple(x) for x in product(range(m), repeat=n)]
    com = otp_com(m)

    T: QuerySet = frozenset({0})  # open coordinate 0 only
    u: String = (1, 0, 2)
    v: String = (1, 2, 1)  # agrees with u on T, differs elsewhere
    print(f"    alphabet Z/{m},  coordinates {{0,1,2}},  opened set T = {set(T)}")
    print(f"    u = {u}   v = {v}   (u and v agree on T)")

    # the hiding bijection e(rho) = rho + (u - v)
    shift: String = tuple((a - b) % m for a, b in zip(u, v))
    print(f"    hiding bijection: e(rho) = rho + (u - v),  u - v = {shift}")

    ok = True
    for rho in pads:
        e_rho: String = tuple((r + s) % m for r, s in zip(rho, shift))
        ok &= com(u, rho) == com(v, e_rho)
        ok &= otp_open(u, rho, T) == otp_open(v, e_rho, T)
    print(f"    commitment AND openings preserved for all {len(pads)} pads: {ok}")

    # and the openings really are informative
    rho0: String = (2, 2, 2)
    c0 = com(u, rho0)
    revealed = otp_open(u, rho0, T)
    recovered = tuple(
        (c0[i] - revealed[i]) % m if revealed[i] is not None else None for i in range(n)
    )
    print(f"    openings are informative: from commitment {c0} and pad {revealed}")
    print(f"      the verifier recovers u|_T = {recovered}  (true u|_T = {restrict_to(T,u)})")
    assert ok and recovered == restrict_to(T, u)
    print()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ingredient 2: sharp 2-transitivity of Sym(Z/3)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def all_perms_of_3() -> List[Tuple[int, int, int]]:
    """Permutations of {0,1,2}, as tuples pi with pi[x] = image of x."""
    return [tuple(p) for p in permutations(range(3))]


def demo_sharp_two_transitivity() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("2.  SHARP 2-TRANSITIVITY OF THE SYMMETRIC GROUP ON THREE LETTERS")
    print("=" * 78)
    perms = all_perms_of_3()
    print(f"    |Sym(Z/3)| = {len(perms)};  ordered pairs of distinct colours = 6")
    all_one = True
    for x, y in product(range(3), repeat=2):
        if x == y:
            continue
        for a, b in product(range(3), repeat=2):
            if a == b:
                continue
            k = sum(1 for pi in perms if pi[x] == a and pi[y] == b)
            all_one &= k == 1
    print(f"    for every distinct (x,y) and distinct (a,b): exactly one permutation? {all_one}")

    # consequence: the opened pair is uniform, whatever the colouring
    print("    induced distribution of the opened pair (pi(c(x)), pi(c(y))):")
    for c_pair in [(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 0)]:
        counts: Dict[Tuple[int, int], int] = {}
        for pi in perms:
            key = (pi[c_pair[0]], pi[c_pair[1]])
            counts[key] = counts.get(key, 0) + 1
        dist = {k: Fraction(v, len(perms)) for k, v in sorted(counts.items())}
        pretty = ", ".join(f"{k}:{v}" for k, v in dist.items())
        print(f"      underlying colours {c_pair} -> {pretty}")
    assert all_one
    print()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. The committed 2-query proof for graph 3-colouring
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def build_three_colouring_protocol(
    colouring: Sequence[int], edges: Sequence[Tuple[int, int]]
) -> CommittedOracle:
    """Prover randomness = the 6 palette permutations; commitment = OTP over Z/3;
    verifier randomness = a uniformly chosen edge; queries = its two endpoints."""
    n = len(colouring)
    perms = all_perms_of_3()
    pads: List[String] = [tuple(x) for x in product(range(3), repeat=n)]

    def proof(pi: Tuple[int, int, int]) -> String:
        return tuple(pi[colouring[v]] for v in range(n))

    def queries(e: Tuple[int, int]) -> QuerySet:
        return frozenset({e[0], e[1]})

    return CommittedOracle(
        n_coords=n,
        com=otp_com(3),
        open_info=otp_open,
        queries=queries,
        qbound=2,
        proof=proof,
        prover_rand=perms,
        commit_rand=pads,
        verifier_rand=list(edges),
    )


def three_colouring_simulator(n: int) -> Tuple[Callable[[object, object], String], List[object]]:
    """The witness-free simulator: on the challenged edge write a uniformly
    random ORDERED PAIR OF DISTINCT COLOURS; 0 elsewhere."""
    sim_rand: List[object] = [
        (a, b) for a, b in product(range(3), repeat=2) if a != b
    ]

    def sim(r: object, s: object) -> String:
        e = r  # the challenged edge
        a, b = s  # the invented distinct colour pair
        out = [0] * n
        out[e[0]] = a
        out[e[1]] = b
        return tuple(out)

    return sim, sim_rand


def demo_three_colouring_hvzk() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("3.  PERFECT ZERO KNOWLEDGE OF THE COMMITTED 2-QUERY 3-COLOURING PROOF")
    print("=" * 78)
    # a properly 3-coloured triangle
    colouring = [0, 1, 2]
    edges = [(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 0)]
    for (x, y) in edges:
        assert colouring[x] != colouring[y], "colouring must be proper"
    print(f"    graph: vertices 0..2, edges {edges}")
    print(f"    proper 3-colouring c = {tuple(colouring)}")

    Pr = build_three_colouring_protocol(colouring, edges)
    sim, sim_rand = three_colouring_simulator(len(colouring))

    print(f"    |P| = {len(Pr.P)} palette permutations, |Rc| = {len(Pr.Rc)} pads, "
          f"|Rv| = {len(Pr.Rv)} edges, |S| = {len(sim_rand)} colour pairs")

    # locality
    max_opened = max(
        len(opened_support(restrict_to(Pr.queries(r), Pr.proof(p))))
        for p in Pr.P
        for r in Pr.Rv
    )
    print(f"    locality: max #symbols exposed by any transcript = {max_opened} (<= q = 2)")

    # completeness
    complete = all(
        Pr.proof(pi)[e[0]] != Pr.proof(pi)[e[1]] for pi in Pr.P for e in Pr.Rv
    )
    print(f"    perfect completeness (opened symbols always differ): {complete}")

    # the two resources
    messages = [Pr.proof(p) for p in Pr.P] + [sim(r, s) for r in Pr.Rv for s in sim_rand]
    print(f"    hiding of unopened coordinates:  {Pr.hides_unopened(messages)}")
    print(f"    perfect simulation of opened view: {Pr.simulates_opened(sim, sim_rand)}")

    # the composition theorem, verified transcript by transcript
    d_real = Pr.real_distribution()
    d_sim = Pr.sim_distribution(sim, sim_rand)
    print(f"    #transcripts with positive real probability: {len(d_real)}")
    print(f"    #transcripts with positive simulated probability: {len(d_sim)}")
    print(f"    distributions identical: {distributions_equal(d_real, d_sim)}")
    print(f"    statistical distance: {statistical_distance(d_real, d_sim)}  (exactly zero)")

    # zero distinguishing advantage for an arbitrary scoring function
    def score(tau: Transcript) -> Fraction:
        c, r, view, o = tau
        return Fraction(sum(x for x in c) * 7 + len(opened_support(view)) * 13 + hash(r) % 5)

    adv = sum(score(t) * d_real.get(t, Fraction(0)) for t in set(d_real) | set(d_sim)) - sum(
        score(t) * d_sim.get(t, Fraction(0)) for t in set(d_real) | set(d_sim)
    )
    print(f"    advantage of an arbitrary (unbounded) distinguisher: {adv}")

    assert distributions_equal(d_real, d_sim) and adv == 0
    print()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Tightness: each hypothesis is necessary
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def demo_hiding_is_necessary() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("4a. HIDING IS NECESSARY (opened view simulated perfectly, yet ZK fails)")
    print("=" * 78)
    # I = {0,1}, A = Z/2, identity 'commitment', query set always {0}
    proof_str: String = (0, 1)

    Pr = CommittedOracle(
        n_coords=2,
        com=lambda u, rho: u,          # publishes the whole string!
        open_info=lambda u, rho, T: 0,  # trivial opening data
        queries=lambda r: frozenset({0}),
        qbound=1,
        proof=lambda p: proof_str,
        prover_rand=[0],
        commit_rand=[0],
        verifier_rand=[0],
    )
    sim_rand: List[object] = [0]
    sim: Callable[[object, object], String] = lambda r, s: (0, 0)

    print(f"    proof string {proof_str}; only coordinate 0 is ever queried")
    print(f"    opened view perfectly simulated: {Pr.simulates_opened(sim, sim_rand)}")
    print(f"    hiding of unopened coordinates:  "
          f"{Pr.hides_unopened([proof_str, (0, 0)])}   <-- FAILS")

    d_real = Pr.real_distribution()
    d_sim = Pr.sim_distribution(sim, sim_rand)
    tau = Pr.real_transcript(0, 0, 0)
    print(f"    honest transcript probability: real = {d_real.get(tau, Fraction(0))}, "
          f"simulated = {d_sim.get(tau, Fraction(0))}")
    print(f"    statistical distance: {statistical_distance(d_real, d_sim)} (maximal)")
    assert d_real[tau] == 1 and d_sim.get(tau, Fraction(0)) == 0
    print()


def demo_simulation_is_necessary() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("4b. SIMULATION IS NECESSARY (perfectly hiding, yet ZK fails)")
    print("=" * 78)
    # I = {0}, A = Z/2, one-time pad, proof string constantly 0
    pads: List[String] = [(0,), (1,)]
    Pr = CommittedOracle(
        n_coords=1,
        com=otp_com(2),
        open_info=otp_open,
        queries=lambda r: frozenset({0}),
        qbound=1,
        proof=lambda p: (0,),
        prover_rand=[0],
        commit_rand=pads,
        verifier_rand=[0],
    )
    sim_rand: List[object] = [0]
    sim: Callable[[object, object], String] = lambda r, s: (1,)  # wrong colour!

    print("    one-coordinate one-time-padded protocol, proof string (0,)")
    print(f"    hiding of unopened coordinates: {Pr.hides_unopened([(0,), (1,)])}")
    print(f"    opened view simulated:          {Pr.simulates_opened(sim, sim_rand)}"
          "   <-- FAILS (simulator opens 1, not 0)")

    d_real = Pr.real_distribution()
    d_sim = Pr.sim_distribution(sim, sim_rand)
    tau = Pr.real_transcript(0, (0,), 0)
    print(f"    a real transcript's probability: real = {d_real.get(tau, Fraction(0))}, "
          f"simulated = {d_sim.get(tau, Fraction(0))}")
    print(f"    statistical distance: {statistical_distance(d_real, d_sim)}")
    assert d_real[tau] == Fraction(1, 2) and d_sim.get(tau, Fraction(0)) == 0
    print()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Transitivity is not enough: cyclic rerandomization leaks
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def demo_cyclic_leaks() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("5.  TRANSITIVITY IS NOT ENOUGH: CYCLIC RERANDOMIZATION ADMITS NO SIMULATOR")
    print("=" * 78)
    edges = [(0, 1)]
    pads: List[String] = [tuple(x) for x in product(range(3), repeat=2)]

    def shift_protocol(colouring: Sequence[int]) -> CommittedOracle:
        return CommittedOracle(
            n_coords=2,
            com=otp_com(3),
            open_info=otp_open,
            queries=lambda r: frozenset({0, 1}),
            qbound=2,
            proof=lambda d: tuple((colouring[v] + d) % 3 for v in range(2)),
            prover_rand=[0, 1, 2],       # the three cyclic shifts
            commit_rand=pads,
            verifier_rand=list(edges),
        )

    A, B = (0, 1), (0, 2)
    PrA, PrB = shift_protocol(A), shift_protocol(B)
    target: PartialView = (0, 1)  # opened view "colour 0 here, colour 1 there"

    def view_prob(Pr: CommittedOracle) -> Fraction:
        T = Pr.queries(edges[0])
        k = sum(1 for d in Pr.P if restrict_to(T, Pr.proof(d)) == target)
        return Fraction(k, len(Pr.P))

    pa, pb = view_prob(PrA), view_prob(PrB)
    print(f"    colouring A = {A}: P[opened view = (0,1)] = {pa}")
    print(f"    colouring B = {B}: P[opened view = (0,1)] = {pb}")
    print("    a simulator never sees the colouring, so it induces ONE number here;")
    print(f"    it would have to equal both {pa} and {pb} -- impossible.")
    print("    => no simulator over any randomness space works for both colourings.")

    # by contrast, with the FULL symmetric group both are 1/6
    def perm_view_prob(colouring: Sequence[int]) -> Fraction:
        perms = all_perms_of_3()
        k = sum(
            1
            for pi in perms
            if (pi[colouring[0]], pi[colouring[1]]) == (0, 1)
        )
        return Fraction(k, len(perms))

    print(f"    with the FULL symmetric group: A -> {perm_view_prob(A)}, "
          f"B -> {perm_view_prob(B)}  (equal, hence simulatable)")
    assert pa != pb and perm_view_prob(A) == perm_view_prob(B)
    print()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Locality: the fibrewise decomposition
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def demo_fibrewise_decomposition() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("6.  FIBREWISE DECOMPOSITION:  count(tau) = #{p : view matches} x fibre count")
    print("=" * 78)
    colouring = [0, 1, 2]
    edges = [(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 0)]
    Pr = build_three_colouring_protocol(colouring, edges)

    checked = 0
    worst = 0
    for p, rho, r in product(Pr.P[:2], Pr.Rc[:4], Pr.Rv[:2]):
        tau = Pr.real_transcript(p, rho, r)
        c, r0, t, o = tau
        T = Pr.queries(r0)
        # brute-force count
        brute = sum(
            1
            for pp, rr, rv in product(Pr.P, Pr.Rc, Pr.Rv)
            if Pr.real_transcript(pp, rr, rv) == tau
        )
        # decomposed count
        matching = [pp for pp in Pr.P if restrict_to(T, Pr.proof(pp)) == t]
        fibres = {Pr.fiber_count(Pr.proof(pp), T, c, o) for pp in matching}
        assert len(fibres) == 1, "hiding should flatten the fibre count"
        N = fibres.pop()
        decomposed = len(matching) * N
        assert brute == decomposed
        checked += 1
        worst = max(worst, brute)
    print(f"    verified count(tau) = |F| x N on {checked} transcripts")
    print("    the fibre count N is CONSTANT across the fibre (this is hiding),")
    print("    and |F| depends only on the <= 2 opened coordinates (this is locality).")
    print(f"    largest transcript count encountered: {worst}")
    print()

def main() -> None:
    print()
    print("COMMITTED LOCAL-ORACLE PROTOCOLS")
    print("Exact composition of PCP locality with commitment hiding")
    print("All probabilities are exact rationals; all claims are checked by enumeration.")
    print()
    demo_one_time_pad_hiding()
    demo_sharp_two_transitivity()
    demo_three_colouring_hvzk()
    demo_hiding_is_necessary()
    demo_simulation_is_necessary()
    demo_cyclic_leaks()
    demo_fibrewise_decomposition()
    print("=" * 78)
    print("ALL DEMONSTRATIONS PASSED.")
    print("=" * 78)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

from __future__ import annotations

from fractions import Fraction
from itertools import permutations, product
from typing import Callable, Dict, FrozenSet, Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Basic types
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Coord = int                      # a coordinate i in I
Symbol = int                     # a symbol a in A
String = Tuple[Symbol, ...]      # a full proof string u : I -> A (indexed by position)
PartialView = Tuple[object, ...] # a partial assignment, None off the query set
QuerySet = FrozenSet[Coord]
Transcript = Tuple[object, object, PartialView, object]


def restrict_to(query: QuerySet, f: String) -> PartialView:
    """The partial view f|_T : None outside T, f(i) inside T."""
    return tuple(f[i] if i in query else None for i in range(len(f)))


def opened_support(view: PartialView) -> List[int]:
    """Coordinates on which a partial view is defined."""
    return [i for i, a in enumerate(view) if a is not None]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A committed local-oracle protocol
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class CommittedOracle:
    """A committed local-oracle protocol over finite randomness spaces.

    com        : (String, Rc) -> C
    open_info  : (String, Rc, QuerySet) -> O
    queries    : Rv -> QuerySet         with |Q(r)| <= qbound
    proof      : P -> String
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        n_coords: int,
        com: Callable[[String, object], object],
        open_info: Callable[[String, object, QuerySet], object],
        queries: Callable[[object], QuerySet],
        qbound: int,
        proof: Callable[[object], String],
        prover_rand: Sequence[object],
        commit_rand: Sequence[object],
        verifier_rand: Sequence[object],
    ) -> None:
        self.n_coords = n_coords
        self.com = com
        self.open_info = open_info
        self.queries = queries
        self.qbound = qbound
        self.proof = proof
        self.P = list(prover_rand)
        self.Rc = list(commit_rand)
        self.Rv = list(verifier_rand)
        for r in self.Rv:
            assert len(self.queries(r)) <= self.qbound, "query bound violated"

    # -- transcripts -------------------------------------------------------

    def real_transcript(self, p: object, rho: object, r: object) -> Transcript:
        u = self.proof(p)
        T = self.queries(r)
        return (self.com(u, rho), r, restrict_to(T, u), self.open_info(u, rho, T))

    def sim_transcript(
        self, sim: Callable[[object, object], String], s: object, rho: object, r: object
    ) -> Transcript:
        u = sim(r, s)
        T = self.queries(r)
        return (self.com(u, rho), r, restrict_to(T, u), self.open_info(u, rho, T))

    # -- exact distributions ----------------------------------------------

    def real_distribution(self) -> Dict[Transcript, Fraction]:
        total = len(self.P) * len(self.Rc) * len(self.Rv)
        counts: Dict[Transcript, int] = {}
        for p, rho, r in product(self.P, self.Rc, self.Rv):
            tau = self.real_transcript(p, rho, r)
            counts[tau] = counts.get(tau, 0) + 1
        return {t: Fraction(c, total) for t, c in counts.items()}

    def sim_distribution(
        self, sim: Callable[[object, object], String], sim_rand: Sequence[object]
    ) -> Dict[Transcript, Fraction]:
        total = len(sim_rand) * len(self.Rc) * len(self.Rv)
        counts: Dict[Transcript, int] = {}
        for s, rho, r in product(sim_rand, self.Rc, self.Rv):
            tau = self.sim_transcript(sim, s, rho, r)
            counts[tau] = counts.get(tau, 0) + 1
        return {t: Fraction(c, total) for t, c in counts.items()}

    # -- the two resources -------------------------------------------------

    def fiber_count(self, u: String, T: QuerySet, c: object, o: object) -> int:
        """#{rho : com(u,rho)=c and open(u,rho,T)=o}."""
        return sum(
            1
            for rho in self.Rc
            if self.com(u, rho) == c and self.open_info(u, rho, T) == o
        )

    def hides_unopened(self, messages: Iterable[String]) -> bool:
        """Check Definition: for all T and all u,v agreeing on T, the fibre
        counts of u and v coincide for every (c,o).  (This is exactly the
        consequence of the hiding bijection that the composition theorem uses,
        and by a counting argument it is equivalent to it over finite Rc.)"""
        msgs = list(messages)
        all_T = [self.queries(r) for r in self.Rv]
        for T in all_T:
            for u, v in product(msgs, msgs):
                if any(u[i] != v[i] for i in T):
                    continue
                pairs = {(self.com(u, rho), self.open_info(u, rho, T)) for rho in self.Rc}
                pairs |= {(self.com(v, rho), self.open_info(v, rho, T)) for rho in self.Rc}
                for (c, o) in pairs:
                    if self.fiber_count(u, T, c, o) != self.fiber_count(v, T, c, o):
                        return False
        return True

    def simulates_opened(
        self, sim: Callable[[object, object], String], sim_rand: Sequence[object]
    ) -> bool:
        """Check  N_real(r,t)*|S| == N_sim(r,t)*|P|  for all r and all views t."""
        nP, nS = len(self.P), len(sim_rand)
        for r in self.Rv:
            T = self.queries(r)
            real: Dict[PartialView, int] = {}
            for p in self.P:
                t = restrict_to(T, self.proof(p))
                real[t] = real.get(t, 0) + 1
            fake: Dict[PartialView, int] = {}
            for s in sim_rand:
                t = restrict_to(T, sim(r, s))
                fake[t] = fake.get(t, 0) + 1
            for t in set(real) | set(fake):
                if real.get(t, 0) * nS != fake.get(t, 0) * nP:
                    return False
        return True


def distributions_equal(
    d1: Dict[Transcript, Fraction], d2: Dict[Transcript, Fraction]
) -> bool:
    return all(d1.get(t, Fraction(0)) == d2.get(t, Fraction(0)) for t in set(d1) | set(d2))


def statistical_distance(
    d1: Dict[Transcript, Fraction], d2: Dict[Transcript, Fraction]
) -> Fraction:
    return sum(
        abs(d1.get(t, Fraction(0)) - d2.get(t, Fraction(0))) for t in set(d1) | set(d2)
    ) / 2


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ingredient 1: the coordinate-wise one-time pad
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def otp_com(modulus: int) -> Callable[[String, String], String]:
    def com(u: String, rho: String) -> String:
        return tuple((a + b) % modulus for a, b in zip(u, rho))

    return com


def otp_open(u: String, rho: String, T: QuerySet) -> PartialView:
    """Opening data = the pad revealed on the queried set."""
    return restrict_to(T, rho)


def demo_one_time_pad_hiding() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("1.  THE ONE-TIME PAD PERFECTLY HIDES UNOPENED COORDINATES")
    print("=" * 78)
    m, n = 3, 3  # alphabet Z/3, three coordinates
    pads: List[String] = [tuple(x) for x in product(range(m), repeat=n)]
    com = otp_com(m)

    T: QuerySet = frozenset({0})  # open coordinate 0 only
    u: String = (1, 0, 2)
    v: String = (1, 2, 1)  # agrees with u on T, differs elsewhere
    print(f"    alphabet Z/{m},  coordinates {{0,1,2}},  opened set T = {set(T)}")
    print(f"    u = {u}   v = {v}   (u and v agree on T)")

    # the hiding bijection e(rho) = rho + (u - v)
    shift: String = tuple((a - b) % m for a, b in zip(u, v))
    print(f"    hiding bijection: e(rho) = rho + (u - v),  u - v = {shift}")

    ok = True
    for rho in pads:
        e_rho: String = tuple((r + s) % m for r, s in zip(rho, shift))
        ok &= com(u, rho) == com(v, e_rho)
        ok &= otp_open(u, rho, T) == otp_open(v, e_rho, T)
    print(f"    commitment AND openings preserved for all {len(pads)} pads: {ok}")

    # and the openings really are informative
    rho0: String = (2, 2, 2)
    c0 = com(u, rho0)
    revealed = otp_open(u, rho0, T)
    recovered = tuple(
        (c0[i] - revealed[i]) % m if revealed[i] is not None else None for i in range(n)
    )
    print(f"    openings are informative: from commitment {c0} and pad {revealed}")
    print(f"      the verifier recovers u|_T = {recovered}  (true u|_T = {restrict_to(T,u)})")
    assert ok and recovered == restrict_to(T, u)
    print()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ingredient 2: sharp 2-transitivity of Sym(Z/3)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def all_perms_of_3() -> List[Tuple[int, int, int]]:
    """Permutations of {0,1,2}, as tuples pi with pi[x] = image of x."""
    return [tuple(p) for p in permutations(range(3))]


def demo_sharp_two_transitivity() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("2.  SHARP 2-TRANSITIVITY OF THE SYMMETRIC GROUP ON THREE LETTERS")
    print("=" * 78)
    perms = all_perms_of_3()
    print(f"    |Sym(Z/3)| = {len(perms)};  ordered pairs of distinct colours = 6")
    all_one = True
    for x, y in product(range(3), repeat=2):
        if x == y:
            continue
        for a, b in product(range(3), repeat=2):
            if a == b:
                continue
            k = sum(1 for pi in perms if pi[x] == a and pi[y] == b)
            all_one &= k == 1
    print(f"    for every distinct (x,y) and distinct (a,b): exactly one permutation? {all_one}")

    # consequence: the opened pair is uniform, whatever the colouring
    print("    induced distribution of the opened pair (pi(c(x)), pi(c(y))):")
    for c_pair in [(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 0)]:
        counts: Dict[Tuple[int, int], int] = {}
        for pi in perms:
            key = (pi[c_pair[0]], pi[c_pair[1]])
            counts[key] = counts.get(key, 0) + 1
        dist = {k: Fraction(v, len(perms)) for k, v in sorted(counts.items())}
        pretty = ", ".join(f"{k}:{v}" for k, v in dist.items())
        print(f"      underlying colours {c_pair} -> {pretty}")
    assert all_one
    print()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. The committed 2-query proof for graph 3-colouring
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def build_three_colouring_protocol(
    colouring: Sequence[int], edges: Sequence[Tuple[int, int]]
) -> CommittedOracle:
    """Prover randomness = the 6 palette permutations; commitment = OTP over Z/3;
    verifier randomness = a uniformly chosen edge; queries = its two endpoints."""
    n = len(colouring)
    perms = all_perms_of_3()
    pads: List[String] = [tuple(x) for x in product(range(3), repeat=n)]

    def proof(pi: Tuple[int, int, int]) -> String:
        return tuple(pi[colouring[v]] for v in range(n))

    def queries(e: Tuple[int, int]) -> QuerySet:
        return frozenset({e[0], e[1]})

    return CommittedOracle(
        n_coords=n,
        com=otp_com(3),
        open_info=otp_open,
        queries=queries,
        qbound=2,
        proof=proof,
        prover_rand=perms,
        commit_rand=pads,
        verifier_rand=list(edges),
    )


def three_colouring_simulator(n: int) -> Tuple[Callable[[object, object], String], List[object]]:
    """The witness-free simulator: on the challenged edge write a uniformly
    random ORDERED PAIR OF DISTINCT COLOURS; 0 elsewhere."""
    sim_rand: List[object] = [
        (a, b) for a, b in product(range(3), repeat=2) if a != b
    ]

    def sim(r: object, s: object) -> String:
        e = r  # the challenged edge
        a, b = s  # the invented distinct colour pair
        out = [0] * n
        out[e[0]] = a
        out[e[1]] = b
        return tuple(out)

    return sim, sim_rand


def demo_three_colouring_hvzk() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("3.  PERFECT ZERO KNOWLEDGE OF THE COMMITTED 2-QUERY 3-COLOURING PROOF")
    print("=" * 78)
    # a properly 3-coloured triangle
    colouring = [0, 1, 2]
    edges = [(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 0)]
    for (x, y) in edges:
        assert colouring[x] != colouring[y], "colouring must be proper"
    print(f"    graph: vertices 0..2, edges {edges}")
    print(f"    proper 3-colouring c = {tuple(colouring)}")

    Pr = build_three_colouring_protocol(colouring, edges)
    sim, sim_rand = three_colouring_simulator(len(colouring))

    print(f"    |P| = {len(Pr.P)} palette permutations, |Rc| = {len(Pr.Rc)} pads, "
          f"|Rv| = {len(Pr.Rv)} edges, |S| = {len(sim_rand)} colour pairs")

    # locality
    max_opened = max(
        len(opened_support(restrict_to(Pr.queries(r), Pr.proof(p))))
        for p in Pr.P
        for r in Pr.Rv
    )
    print(f"    locality: max #symbols exposed by any transcript = {max_opened} (<= q = 2)")

    # completeness
    complete = all(
        Pr.proof(pi)[e[0]] != Pr.proof(pi)[e[1]] for pi in Pr.P for e in Pr.Rv
    )
    print(f"    perfect completeness (opened symbols always differ): {complete}")

    # the two resources
    messages = [Pr.proof(p) for p in Pr.P] + [sim(r, s) for r in Pr.Rv for s in sim_rand]
    print(f"    hiding of unopened coordinates:  {Pr.hides_unopened(messages)}")
    print(f"    perfect simulation of opened view: {Pr.simulates_opened(sim, sim_rand)}")

    # the composition theorem, verified transcript by transcript
    d_real = Pr.real_distribution()
    d_sim = Pr.sim_distribution(sim, sim_rand)
    print(f"    #transcripts with positive real probability: {len(d_real)}")
    print(f"    #transcripts with positive simulated probability: {len(d_sim)}")
    print(f"    distributions identical: {distributions_equal(d_real, d_sim)}")
    print(f"    statistical distance: {statistical_distance(d_real, d_sim)}  (exactly zero)")

    # zero distinguishing advantage for an arbitrary scoring function
    def score(tau: Transcript) -> Fraction:
        c, r, view, o = tau
        return Fraction(sum(x for x in c) * 7 + len(opened_support(view)) * 13 + hash(r) % 5)

    adv = sum(score(t) * d_real.get(t, Fraction(0)) for t in set(d_real) | set(d_sim)) - sum(
        score(t) * d_sim.get(t, Fraction(0)) for t in set(d_real) | set(d_sim)
    )
    print(f"    advantage of an arbitrary (unbounded) distinguisher: {adv}")

    assert distributions_equal(d_real, d_sim) and adv == 0
    print()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Tightness: each hypothesis is necessary
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def demo_hiding_is_necessary() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("4a. HIDING IS NECESSARY (opened view simulated perfectly, yet ZK fails)")
    print("=" * 78)
    # I = {0,1}, A = Z/2, identity 'commitment', query set always {0}
    proof_str: String = (0, 1)

    Pr = CommittedOracle(
        n_coords=2,
        com=lambda u, rho: u,          # publishes the whole string!
        open_info=lambda u, rho, T: 0,  # trivial opening data
        queries=lambda r: frozenset({0}),
        qbound=1,
        proof=lambda p: proof_str,
        prover_rand=[0],
        commit_rand=[0],
        verifier_rand=[0],
    )
    sim_rand: List[object] = [0]
    sim: Callable[[object, object], String] = lambda r, s: (0, 0)

    print(f"    proof string {proof_str}; only coordinate 0 is ever queried")
    print(f"    opened view perfectly simulated: {Pr.simulates_opened(sim, sim_rand)}")
    print(f"    hiding of unopened coordinates:  "
          f"{Pr.hides_unopened([proof_str, (0, 0)])}   <-- FAILS")

    d_real = Pr.real_distribution()
    d_sim = Pr.sim_distribution(sim, sim_rand)
    tau = Pr.real_transcript(0, 0, 0)
    print(f"    honest transcript probability: real = {d_real.get(tau, Fraction(0))}, "
          f"simulated = {d_sim.get(tau, Fraction(0))}")
    print(f"    statistical distance: {statistical_distance(d_real, d_sim)} (maximal)")
    assert d_real[tau] == 1 and d_sim.get(tau, Fraction(0)) == 0
    print()


def demo_simulation_is_necessary() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("4b. SIMULATION IS NECESSARY (perfectly hiding, yet ZK fails)")
    print("=" * 78)
    # I = {0}, A = Z/2, one-time pad, proof string constantly 0
    pads: List[String] = [(0,), (1,)]
    Pr = CommittedOracle(
        n_coords=1,
        com=otp_com(2),
        open_info=otp_open,
        queries=lambda r: frozenset({0}),
        qbound=1,
        proof=lambda p: (0,),
        prover_rand=[0],
        commit_rand=pads,
        verifier_rand=[0],
    )
    sim_rand: List[object] = [0]
    sim: Callable[[object, object], String] = lambda r, s: (1,)  # wrong colour!

    print("    one-coordinate one-time-padded protocol, proof string (0,)")
    print(f"    hiding of unopened coordinates: {Pr.hides_unopened([(0,), (1,)])}")
    print(f"    opened view simulated:          {Pr.simulates_opened(sim, sim_rand)}"
          "   <-- FAILS (simulator opens 1, not 0)")

    d_real = Pr.real_distribution()
    d_sim = Pr.sim_distribution(sim, sim_rand)
    tau = Pr.real_transcript(0, (0,), 0)
    print(f"    a real transcript's probability: real = {d_real.get(tau, Fraction(0))}, "
          f"simulated = {d_sim.get(tau, Fraction(0))}")
    print(f"    statistical distance: {statistical_distance(d_real, d_sim)}")
    assert d_real[tau] == Fraction(1, 2) and d_sim.get(tau, Fraction(0)) == 0
    print()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Transitivity is not enough: cyclic rerandomization leaks
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def demo_cyclic_leaks() -> None:

def marginal(group: Sequence[Perm], colouring: Sequence[int], T: QuerySet) -> Dict[PartialView, Fraction]:

from fractions import Fraction

from typing import Callable, Dict, FrozenSet, List, Sequence, Tuple

String = Tuple[int, ...]
PartialView = Tuple[object, ...]
QuerySet = FrozenSet[int]
Transcript = Tuple[object, object, PartialView, object]


def restrict_to(query: QuerySet, f: String) -> PartialView:
    """Partial view f|_T: the symbol f(i) inside T, None outside T."""
    return tuple(f[i] if i in query else None for i in range(len(f)))


def transcript_distribution(
    com: Callable[[String, object], object],
    open_info: Callable[[String, object, QuerySet], object],
    queries: Callable[[object], QuerySet],
    string_of: Callable[[object, object], String],
    coin_space: Sequence[object],
    commit_rand: Sequence[object],
    verifier_rand: Sequence[object],
) -> Dict[Transcript, Fraction]:
    """Exact distribution over transcripts.

    `string_of(r, w)` returns the committed string for verifier coins `r` and
    party randomness `w`.  For the real interaction this ignores `r` and returns
    proof(w); for the simulator it is sim(r, w).  This uniform interface lets one
    routine serve both sides.
    """
    total = len(coin_space) * len(commit_rand) * len(verifier_rand)
    counts: Dict[Transcript, int] = {}
    for w, rho, r in product(coin_space, commit_rand, verifier_rand):
        u = string_of(r, w)
        T = queries(r)
        tau: Transcript = (com(u, rho), r, restrict_to(T, u), open_info(u, rho, T))
        counts[tau] = counts.get(tau, 0) + 1
    return {t: Fraction(c, total) for t, c in counts.items()}

    d_real: Dict[Transcript, Fraction], d_sim: Dict[Transcript, Fraction]
) -> Tuple[bool, Fraction, List[Transcript]]:
    """Return (identical?, statistical distance, list of witnessing transcripts)."""
    support = set(d_real) | set(d_sim)
    zero = Fraction(0)
    witnesses = [t for t in support if d_real.get(t, zero) != d_sim.get(t, zero)]
    dist = sum(abs(d_real.get(t, zero) - d_sim.get(t, zero)) for t in support) / 2
    return (not witnesses), Fraction(dist), sorted(witnesses, key=repr)[:5]


def is_perfect_hvzk(
    com: Callable[[String, object], object],
    open_info: Callable[[String, object, QuerySet], object],
    queries: Callable[[object], QuerySet],
    proof: Callable[[object], String],

    commit_rand: Sequence[object],
    verifier_rand: Sequence[object],

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import permutations, product
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple

Perm = Tuple[int, ...]          # perm[x] = image of x
Tuple_ = Tuple[int, ...]


def symmetric_group(n: int) -> List[Perm]:
    """All n! permutations of {0, ..., n-1}."""
    return [tuple(p) for p in permutations(range(n))]


def cyclic_group(n: int) -> List[Perm]:
    """The n cyclic shifts x -> x + d (mod n)."""
    return [tuple((x + d) % n for x in range(n)) for d in range(n)]


def admissible_tuples(
    alphabet_size: int, arity: int, constraint: Callable[[Tuple_], bool]
) -> List[Tuple_]:
    """All symbol tuples of the given arity satisfying the local constraint."""
    return [t for t in product(range(alphabet_size), repeat=arity) if constraint(t)]


def orbit_multiplicities(
    group: Sequence[Perm], base: Tuple_
) -> Dict[Tuple_, int]:
    """Multiset of images g.base for g in the group."""
    mult: Dict[Tuple_, int] = {}
    for g in group:
        image = tuple(g[x] for x in base)
        mult[image] = mult.get(image, 0) + 1
    return mult


def certify_sharp_transitivity(
    group: Sequence[Perm],
    alphabet_size: int,
    arity: int,
    constraint: Callable[[Tuple_], bool],
) -> Dict[str, object]:

    Returns a report dictionary with the verdict and the offending multiplicities.

        "num_admissible": len(targets),
        "transitive": True,
        "sharply_transitive": True,
        "worst_base": None,
        "multiplicities": {},

from __future__ import annotations

from fractions import Fraction
from typing import Callable, Dict, FrozenSet, List, Sequence, Tuple

String = Tuple[int, ...]
PartialView = Tuple[object, ...]
QuerySet = FrozenSet[int]


def restrict_to(query: QuerySet, f: String) -> PartialView:
    return tuple(f[i] if i in query else None for i in range(len(f)))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# B. fibre-count profiler
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def fibre_count(
    com: Callable[[String, object], object],
    open_info: Callable[[String, object, QuerySet], object],
    commit_rand: Sequence[object],
    u: String,
    T: QuerySet,
    c: object,
    o: object,
) -> int:
    """#{rho : com(u,rho) = c and open(u,rho,T) = o}."""
    return sum(
        1 for rho in commit_rand if com(u, rho) == c and open_info(u, rho, T) == o
    )


def profile_hiding(
    com: Callable[[String, object], object],
    open_info: Callable[[String, object, QuerySet], object],
    commit_rand: Sequence[object],
    messages: Sequence[String],
    T: QuerySet,
) -> Tuple[bool, List[Tuple[String, String, object, object, int, int]]]:
    """Check fibre-count constancy on each 'agrees on T' class.

    Returns (hiding_ok, list of violations (u, v, c, o, fib_u, fib_v)).
    """
    violations: List[Tuple[String, String, object, object, int, int]] = []
    for u in messages:
        for v in messages:
            if any(u[i] != v[i] for i in T):
                continue
            observables = {(com(u, rho), open_info(u, rho, T)) for rho in commit_rand}
            observables |= {(com(v, rho), open_info(v, rho, T)) for rho in commit_rand}
            for (c, o) in observables:
                fu = fibre_count(com, open_info, commit_rand, u, T, c, o)
                fv = fibre_count(com, open_info, commit_rand, v, T, c, o)
                if fu != fv:
                    violations.append((u, v, c, o, fu, fv))
    return (not violations), violations[:5]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# C. local-view marginal checker
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def local_marginal(
    strings: Sequence[String], T: QuerySet
) -> Dict[PartialView, int]:
    """The q-marginal: how many coin values give each opened view."""
    table: Dict[PartialView, int] = {}
    for u in strings:
        t = restrict_to(T, u)
        table[t] = table.get(t, 0) + 1
    return table


def check_simulation(
    queries: Callable[[object], QuerySet],
    proof: Callable[[object], String],
    sim: Callable[[object, object], String],
    prover_rand: Sequence[object],
    sim_rand: Sequence[object],
    verifier_rand: Sequence[object],
) -> Tuple[bool, List[Tuple[object, PartialView, Fraction, Fraction]]]:
    """Verify N_real(r,t)*|S| = N_sim(r,t)*|P| for all r, t.

    Returns (ok, list of mismatches (r, t, real prob, sim prob)).
    """
    nP, nS = len(prover_rand), len(sim_rand)
    bad: List[Tuple[object, PartialView, Fraction, Fraction]] = []
    for r in verifier_rand:
        T = queries(r)
        real = local_marginal([proof(p) for p in prover_rand], T)
        fake = local_marginal([sim(r, s) for s in sim_rand], T)
        for t in set(real) | set(fake):
            if real.get(t, 0) * nS != fake.get(t, 0) * nP:
                bad.append((r, t, Fraction(real.get(t, 0), nP), Fraction(fake.get(t, 0), nS)))
    return (not bad), bad[:5]

def restrict_to(query: QuerySet, f: String) -> PartialView:

def distribution(
    com: Callable[[String, object], object],
    open_info: Callable[[String, object, QuerySet], object],
    queries: Callable[[object], QuerySet],
    string_of: Callable[[object, object], String],
    coins: Sequence[object],
    commit_rand: Sequence[object],
    verifier_rand: Sequence[object],
) -> Dict[Transcript, Fraction]:
    total = len(coins) * len(commit_rand) * len(verifier_rand)
    counts: Dict[Transcript, int] = {}
    for w, rho, r in product(coins, commit_rand, verifier_rand):
        u = string_of(r, w)
        T = queries(r)
        tau = (com(u, rho), r, restrict_to(T, u), open_info(u, rho, T))
        counts[tau] = counts.get(tau, 0) + 1
    return {t: Fraction(c, total) for t, c in counts.items()}


def three_colouring_case() -> Tuple[Dict[Transcript, Fraction], Dict[Transcript, Fraction]]:
    colouring = (0, 1, 2)

    pads: List[object] = [tuple(x) for x in product(range(3), repeat=3)]
    pairs: List[object] = [(a, b) for a in range(3) for b in range(3) if a != b]

    com = lambda u, rho: tuple((a + b) % 3 for a, b in zip(u, rho))
    open_info = lambda u, rho, T: restrict_to(T, rho)
    queries = lambda r: frozenset({r[0], r[1]})
    proof = lambda r, pi: tuple(pi[colouring[v]] for v in range(3))
    sim = lambda r, s: tuple(
        s[0] if v == r[0] else s[1] if v == r[1] else 0 for v in range(3)
    )
    return (
        distribution(com, open_info, queries, proof, perms, pads, edges),
        distribution(com, open_info, queries, sim, pairs, pads, edges),
    )

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import permutations
from typing import Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

Perm = Tuple[int, int, int]


def symmetric_group_3() -> List[Perm]:
    return [tuple(p) for p in permutations(range(3))]  # type: ignore[misc]


def cyclic_group_3() -> List[Perm]:
    return [tuple((x + d) % 3 for x in range(3)) for d in range(3)]  # type: ignore[misc]


def distinct_pairs() -> List[Tuple[int, int]]:
    return [(a, b) for a in range(3) for b in range(3) if a != b]


def incidence(group: Sequence[Perm], base: Tuple[int, int]) -> np.ndarray:
    pairs = distinct_pairs()
    M = np.zeros((len(group), len(pairs)))
    for i, g in enumerate(group):
        image = (g[base[0]], g[base[1]])
        if image in pairs:
            M[i][pairs.index(image)] = 1.0
    return M


def plot() -> None:
    pairs = distinct_pairs()
    labels = [f"({a},{b})" for a, b in pairs]

    panels = [
        ("full symmetric group, colours (0,1)", symmetric_group_3(), (0, 1)),
        ("cyclic shifts, colours (0,1)", cyclic_group_3(), (0, 1)),
        ("cyclic shifts, colours (0,2)", cyclic_group_3(), (0, 2)),
    ]

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(15, 7), gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [2, 1]})
    for col, (title, group, base) in enumerate(panels):
        M = incidence(group, base)
        ax = axes[0][col]
        ax.imshow(M, cmap="Blues", vmin=0, vmax=1, aspect="auto")
        ax.set_xticks(range(len(pairs)))
        ax.set_xticklabels(labels, fontsize=9)
        ax.set_yticks(range(len(group)))
        ax.set_yticklabels([str(g) for g in group], fontsize=8)
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=11)
        ax.set_xlabel("opened colour pair")
        ax.set_ylabel("group element")
        for i in range(M.shape[0]):

                    ax.text(j, i, "1", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=8, color="white")

        axd = axes[1][col]
        probs = M.sum(axis=0) / len(group)
        colours = ["#2c6fbb" if p > 0 else "#cccccc" for p in probs]
        axd.bar(range(len(pairs)), probs, color=colours)
        axd.set_xticks(range(len(pairs)))
        axd.set_xticklabels(labels, fontsize=9)
        axd.set_ylim(0, 0.45)
        axd.set_ylabel("probability")
        for j, p in enumerate(probs):
            if p > 0:
                axd.text(j, p + 0.01, f"{p:.2f}", ha="center", fontsize=8)

    fig.suptitle(
        "Sharp 2-transitivity is the simulation resource\n"
        "left: six group elements, six targets, exactly one hit each -- the opened pair is uniform\n"
        "middle/right: cyclic shifts hit different halves for different colourings -- no simulator can match both",
        fontsize=12,
    )
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.88))
    fig.savefig("orbit_incidence.png", dpi=150)
    print("wrote orbit_incidence.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    plot()

    display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;font-size:1.5rem;font-weight:700;
    transition:.28s;border:2px solid #3d4a6e}
  .lid.closed{background:repeating-linear-gradient(45deg,#28324e,#28324e 7px,#222b44 7px,#222b44 14px);
    border:2px solid #3d4a6e;color:#6d7ea3}
  .lid.open{border:2px solid #ffffff33}
  .box .cap{font-size:.72rem;color:var(--muted);margin-top:5px}
  .stat{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;padding:7px 0;border-bottom:1px dashed #2b3550;font-size:.9rem}
  .stat:last-child{border-bottom:none}
  .stat b{font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
  .ok{color:var(--good)} .no{color:var(--bad)} .mid{color:var(--warn)}
  .bars{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(9,1fr);gap:7px;margin-top:10px}
  .bcol{text-align:center}
  .bstack{height:110px;display:flex;align-items:flex-end;justify-content:center;gap:3px}
  .b{width:13px;border-radius:3px 3px 0 0;transition:height .3s}
  .b.real{background:var(--accent)} .b.sim{background:#e2725b}
  .blab{font-size:.63rem;color:var(--muted);margin-top:4px;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
  .legend{display:flex;gap:16px;justify-content:center;font-size:.78rem;color:var(--muted);margin-top:10px}
  .sw{display:inline-block;width:11px;height:11px;border-radius:3px;margin-right:5px;vertical-align:-1px}
  table.inc{border-collapse:collapse;margin:8px auto 0;font-size:.75rem}
  table.inc td,table.inc th{border:1px solid #2b3550;padding:4px 7px;text-align:center;
    font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
  table.inc th{color:var(--muted);font-weight:600}
  table.inc td.hit{background:#2f5fae;color:#fff;font-weight:700}
  table.inc td.miss{color:#42506f}
  .verdict{margin-top:14px;padding:11px 13px;border-radius:10px;font-size:.9rem}
  .verdict.good{background:#0f3b25;border:1px solid #1f6b43;color:#b9f5d2}
  .verdict.bad{background:#3e1420;border:1px solid #7d2740;color:#ffc9d4}
  .note{font-size:.82rem;color:var(--muted);margin-top:12px}
  code{background:#111827;padding:1px 5px;border-radius:4px;font-size:.86em}
  .log{font-family:ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,Menlo,monospace;font-size:.76rem;color:#a9b8d8;
    background:#101725;border:1px solid #232d47;border-radius:9px;padding:9px 11px;height:96px;
    overflow-y:auto;margin-top:12px;white-space:pre-wrap}
</style>

<body>
<div class="wrap">
  <h1>The Committed Local-Oracle Laboratory</h1>
  <p class="sub">Shuffle the palette, seal the boxes, open one edge — and watch perfect zero knowledge
  appear (or fail) as an <em>exact</em> arithmetic identity.</p>

  <div class="grid">
    <!-- ---------------- controls ---------------- -->
    <div>
      <div class="panel">
        <h2>Protocol controls</h2>

        <label class="row"><span>Rerandomization group acting on the palette</span>
          <select id="group">
            <option value="sym">Full symmetric group — all 6 palette permutations</option>
            <option value="cyc">Cyclic shifts only — colour → colour + d (3 elements)</option>
            <option value="swap">Single transposition — swap colours 0 and 1 (2 elements)</option>
            <option value="triv">No shuffle at all (1 element)</option>
          </select>
        </label>

        <label class="row"><span>Secret colouring of the triangle</span>
          <select id="colouring">
            <option value="012">c = (0, 1, 2)</option>
            <option value="120">c = (1, 2, 0)</option>
            <option value="102">c = (1, 0, 2)</option>
          </select>
        </label>

        <label class="row"><span>Challenged edge (the verifier’s coin)</span>
          <select id="edge">
            <option value="01">edge {0, 1}</option>
            <option value="12">edge {1, 2}</option>
            <option value="20">edge {2, 0}</option>
          </select>
        </label>

        <label class="toggle"><input type="checkbox" id="hiding" checked/>
          <span>Commitment hides unopened coordinates (one-time pad)</span></label>

        <div class="btnrow">
          <button class="primary" id="run">Run a round</button>
          <button id="reset">Reseal boxes</button>
        </div>

        <div class="log" id="log"></div>
      </div>

      <div class="panel" style="margin-top:16px">
        <h2>Exact verdict</h2>
        <div class="stat"><span>Query complexity <code>q</code></span><b>2</b></div>
        <div class="stat"><span>Symbols exposed by a transcript</span><b id="exposed">2</b></div>
        <div class="stat"><span>Hiding of unopened coordinates</span><b id="vHide">—</b></div>
        <div class="stat"><span>Simulation of the opened pair</span><b id="vSim">—</b></div>
        <div class="stat"><span>Statistical distance real ↔ simulated</span><b id="vDist">—</b></div>
        <div id="verdict" class="verdict good"> </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <!-- ---------------- stage ---------------- -->
    <div>
      <div class="panel">
        <h2>The prover’s sealed proof string</h2>
        <svg id="graph" width="330" height="180" viewBox="0 0 330 180"></svg>
        <div class="boxes" id="boxes"></div>
        <p class="note" id="stageNote">Press <b>Run a round</b>: the palette is shuffled by a uniformly random
        element of the chosen group, every vertex colour is sealed in its own box, and only the two boxes on
        the challenged edge are opened.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="panel" style="margin-top:16px">
        <h2>Distribution of the opened pair — real interaction vs. witness-free simulator</h2>
        <div class="bars" id="bars"></div>
        <div class="legend">
          <span><i class="sw" style="background:var(--accent)"></i>real prover (knows the colouring)</span>
          <span><i class="sw" style="background:#e2725b"></i>simulator (knows nothing)</span>
        </div>
        <p class="note">The simulator always outputs a uniformly random <em>ordered pair of distinct colours</em>.
        The two spectra coincide exactly when the group acts <b>sharply transitively</b> on those six pairs.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="panel" style="margin-top:16px">
        <h2>Orbit incidence: which group element produces which opened pair</h2>
        <div id="inc"></div>
        <p class="note">One row per group element, one column per admissible opened pair. A permutation matrix
        — exactly one mark per row <em>and</em> per column — is sharp 2-transitivity, and is precisely
        what makes the opened view forgeable without the secret.</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
"use strict";

/* ---------- exact rational arithmetic on small integers ---------- */
function gcd(a,b){a=Math.abs(a);b=Math.abs(b);while(b){[a,b]=[b,a%b];}return a||1;}
function frac(n,d){const g=gcd(n,d);return [n/g,d/g];}
function fracStr(n,d){if(n===0)return "0";const [p,q]=frac(n,d);return q===1?String(p):p+"/"+q;}

/* ---------- groups on the palette {0,1,2} ---------- */
const GROUPS = {
  sym : [[0,1,2],[0,2,1],[1,0,2],[1,2,0],[2,0,1],[2,1,0]],
  cyc : [[0,1,2],[1,2,0],[2,0,1]],
  swap: [[0,1,2],[1,0,2]],
  triv: [[0,1,2]]
};
const GROUP_NAME = {sym:"full symmetric group", cyc:"cyclic shifts",
                    swap:"transposition (0 1)", triv:"trivial group"};
const COLOURS = ["#e05252","#4d9de0","#3fbf7f"];
const PAIRS = [];
for(let a=0;a<3;a++) for(let b=0;b<3;b++) if(a!==b) PAIRS.push([a,b]);

/* ---------- state ---------- */
let state = {
  perm:[0,1,2], pad:[0,0,0], opened:false, ran:false
};

const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
const colouringOf = () => $("colouring").value.split("").map(Number);
const edgeOf      = () => $("edge").value.split("").map(Number);
const groupOf     = () => GROUPS[$("group").value];

/* ---------- the graph ---------- */
const POS = [[60,140],[165,32],[270,140]];
function drawGraph(){
  const c = colouringOf(), e = edgeOf();
  const svg = $("graph");
  let s = "";
  const E = [[0,1],[1,2],[2,0]];
  for(const [x,y] of E){
    const on = (x===e[0]&&y===e[1])||(x===e[1]&&y===e[0]);
    s += `<line x1="${POS[x][0]}" y1="${POS[x][1]}" x2="${POS[y][0]}" y2="${POS[y][1]}"
           stroke="${on?"#6fa8ff":"#2c3550"}" stroke-width="${on?5:2}"
           stroke-linecap="round" opacity="${on?1:.45}"/>`;
  }
  for(let v=0;v<3;v++){
    const shown = state.ran ? state.perm[c[v]] : c[v];
    const hidden = state.ran && !(v===e[0]||v===e[1]);
    s += `<circle cx="${POS[v][0]}" cy="${POS[v][1]}" r="21"
            fill="${hidden?"#2b3550":COLOURS[shown]}"
            stroke="#0f1420" stroke-width="3"/>`;
    s += `<text x="${POS[v][0]}" y="${POS[v][1]+5}" text-anchor="middle"
            font-size="13" font-weight="700" fill="${hidden?"#6d7ea3":"#0f1420"}">${hidden?"?":shown}</text>`;
    s += `<text x="${POS[v][0]}" y="${POS[v][1]+38}" text-anchor="middle"
            font-size="11" fill="#93a2c0">vertex ${v}</text>`;
  }
  svg.innerHTML = s;
}

/* ---------- the boxes ---------- */
function drawBoxes(){
  const c = colouringOf(), e = edgeOf();
  const hiding = $("hiding").checked;
  let s = "";
  for(let v=0;v<3;v++){
    const isOpen = state.ran && (v===e[0]||v===e[1]);
    const sym = state.ran ? state.perm[c[v]] : c[v];
    // with hiding OFF the "commitment" publishes the symbol outright
    const visible = isOpen || !hiding || !state.ran;
    const commit = (sym + state.pad[v] + 3) % 3;
    if(visible){
      s += `<div class="box"><div class="lid open" style="background:${COLOURS[sym]};color:#0f1420">${sym}</div>
            <div class="cap">${isOpen?"opened":(hiding?"":"LEAKED")}</div></div>`;
    }else{
      s += `<div class="box"><div class="lid closed">${hiding?"🔒":commit}</div>
            <div class="cap">sealed</div></div>`;
    }
  }
  $("boxes").innerHTML = s;
}

/* ---------- distributions ---------- */
function realPairCounts(){
  const c = colouringOf(), e = edgeOf(), G = groupOf();
  const counts = {};
  for(const g of G){
    const key = g[c[e[0]]] + "," + g[c[e[1]]];
    counts[key] = (counts[key]||0)+1;
  }
  return {counts, total:G.length};
}
function simPairCounts(){
  const counts = {};
  for(const [a,b] of PAIRS) counts[a+","+b] = 1;
  return {counts, total:PAIRS.length};
}

function drawBars(){
  const R = realPairCounts(), S = simPairCounts();
  // include the three "equal" pairs too, so a degenerate group is visible
  const keys = [];
  for(let a=0;a<3;a++) for(let b=0;b<3;b++) keys.push(a+","+b);
  let html = "";
  for(const k of keys){
    const pr = (R.counts[k]||0)/R.total, ps = (S.counts[k]||0)/S.total;
    html += `<div class="bcol"><div class="bstack">
      <div class="b real" style="height:${Math.round(pr*100)}%"></div>
      <div class="b sim"  style="height:${Math.round(ps*100)}%"></div>
      </div><div class="blab">(${k})</div>
      <div class="blab">${fracStr(R.counts[k]||0,R.total)} / ${fracStr(S.counts[k]||0,S.total)}</div></div>`;
  }
  $("bars").innerHTML = html;
  $("bars").style.gridTemplateColumns = "repeat(9,1fr)";
}

/* ---------- incidence table ---------- */
function drawIncidence(){
  const c = colouringOf(), e = edgeOf(), G = groupOf();
  let h = "<table class='inc'><tr><th>group element</th>";
  for(const [a,b] of PAIRS) h += `<th>(${a},${b})</th>`;
  h += "</tr>";
  for(const g of G){
    const img = [g[c[e[0]]], g[c[e[1]]]];
    h += `<tr><td>[${g.join(" ")}]</td>`;
    for(const [a,b] of PAIRS){
      const hit = img[0]===a && img[1]===b;
      h += `<td class="${hit?"hit":"miss"}">${hit?"1":"·"}</td>`;
    }
    h += "</tr>";
  }
  h += "</table>";
  $("inc").innerHTML = h;
}

/* ---------- exact transcript distributions ---------- */
/* Enumerates the full randomness cube.  With hiding ON the commitment is the
   coordinate-wise one-time pad  com(u,rho) = u + rho  and the opening reveals
   the pad on the queried set.  With hiding OFF the "commitment" publishes the
   whole string.  Everything is counted exactly. */
function transcriptCounts(strings, hiding){
  const pads = [];
  for(let a=0;a<3;a++) for(let b=0;b<3;b++) for(let c=0;c<3;c++) pads.push([a,b,c]);
  const e = edgeOf();
  const counts = {};
  for(const u of strings){
    for(const rho of pads){
      const com = hiding ? u.map((x,i)=>(x+rho[i])%3) : u.slice();
      const view = [0,1,2].map(v => (v===e[0]||v===e[1]) ? u[v] : "-");
      const open = [0,1,2].map(v => (v===e[0]||v===e[1]) ? rho[v] : "-");
      const key = com.join("")+"|"+view.join("")+"|"+open.join("");
      counts[key] = (counts[key]||0)+1;
    }
  }
  return {counts, total: strings.length*pads.length};
}

function realStrings(){
  const c = colouringOf(), G = groupOf();
  return G.map(g => [0,1,2].map(v => g[c[v]]));
}
function simStrings(){
  const e = edgeOf();
  return PAIRS.map(([a,b]) => [0,1,2].map(v => v===e[0] ? a : (v===e[1] ? b : 0)));
}

/* ---------- verdict ---------- */
function updateVerdict(){
  const R = realPairCounts(), S = simPairCounts();
  const keysP = new Set([...Object.keys(R.counts), ...Object.keys(S.counts)]);
  let numP = 0;
  for(const k of keysP)
    numP += Math.abs((R.counts[k]||0)*S.total - (S.counts[k]||0)*R.total);
  const simOK = numP === 0;
  const hideOK = $("hiding").checked;

  /* exact statistical distance between the FULL transcript distributions */
  const TR = transcriptCounts(realStrings(), hideOK);
  const TS = transcriptCounts(simStrings(), hideOK);
  const keysT = new Set([...Object.keys(TR.counts), ...Object.keys(TS.counts)]);
  let numT = 0;
  for(const k of keysT)
    numT += Math.abs((TR.counts[k]||0)*TS.total - (TS.counts[k]||0)*TR.total);
  const denT = 2*TR.total*TS.total;

  $("vHide").textContent = hideOK ? "perfect" : "FAILS";
  $("vHide").className = hideOK ? "ok" : "no";
  $("vSim").textContent = simOK ? "perfect" : "FAILS";
  $("vSim").className = simOK ? "ok" : "no";
  $("vDist").textContent = fracStr(numT, denT);
  $("vDist").className = (numT===0) ? "ok" : "no";

  const v = $("verdict");
  if(hideOK && simOK){
    v.className = "verdict good";
    v.innerHTML = "<b>Perfect honest-verifier zero knowledge.</b> Hiding controls the unopened "+
      "coordinates, sharp 2-transitivity controls the opened pair, and the two compose exactly: "+
      "every transcript has identical probability in the real interaction and in the simulation, "+
      "so the statistical distance is exactly zero.";
  }else if(!hideOK && simOK){
    v.className = "verdict bad";
    v.innerHTML = "<b>Zero knowledge fails — the commitment leaks.</b> The opened pair is still "+
      "perfectly simulated, but the unopened coordinate is published in the clear. The leak is "+
      "invisible in the opened view: simulation alone is not enough.";
  }else if(hideOK && !simOK){
    v.className = "verdict bad";
    v.innerHTML = "<b>Zero knowledge fails — the opened pair is not simulatable.</b> The "+
      GROUP_NAME[$("group").value]+" is not sharply transitive on ordered pairs of distinct colours, "+
      "so the two revealed symbols carry a genuine function of the secret colouring.";
  }else{
    v.className = "verdict bad";
    v.innerHTML = "<b>Both hypotheses fail.</b> The commitment publishes unopened coordinates and the "+
      "opened pair is not uniform: the verifier learns the colouring outright.";
  }
}

/* ---------- interaction ---------- */
function log(msg){
  const el = $("log");
  el.textContent += msg + "\n";
  el.scrollTop = el.scrollHeight;
}

function runRound(){
  const G = groupOf(), c = colouringOf(), e = edgeOf();
  state.perm = G[Math.floor(Math.random()*G.length)];
  state.pad  = [0,1,2].map(()=>Math.floor(Math.random()*3));
  state.ran = true;
  redraw();
  const a = state.perm[c[e[0]]], b = state.perm[c[e[1]]];
  log(`round: shuffle [${state.perm.join(" ")}]  pad (${state.pad.join(",")})  `+
      `edge {${e[0]},${e[1]}}  opened pair (${a},${b})  `+
      `verifier ${a!==b?"ACCEPTS":"REJECTS"}`);
}

function reset(){ state.ran = false; redraw(); }

function redraw(){
  drawGraph(); drawBoxes(); drawBars(); drawIncidence(); updateVerdict();
  $("exposed").textContent = state.ran ? "2" : "0";
}

["group","colouring","edge"].forEach(id=>$(id).addEventListener("change",()=>{state.ran=false;redraw();}));
$("hiding").addEventListener("change",redraw);
$("run").addEventListener("click",runRound);
$("reset").addEventListener("click",reset);
redraw();
log("ready. the secret colouring is never shown to the verifier -- only two symbols per round.");
</script>
</body>
</html>
"
    },
    {
      "title": "The Fibre-Counting Machine",
      "description": "The proof of the composition theorem rendered as a single picture. Fix a transcript — a colouring, a challenged edge, and the pair of colours it records — and the widget displays two randomness cubes stacked one above the other: the real prover's (one row per group element, 27 one-time pads across) and the simulator's (one row per ordered pair of distinct colours). <body>
<div class="wrap">

  count factors as a <b style="color:var(--accent)">horizontal</b> fibre (which coins produce the visible

  published). Hiding makes the vertical factor the <em>same number</em> on both sides; simulation makes the
  horizontal factors proportional. Multiply, and the two probabilities are equal.</p>

  <div class="panel">
